name: Porcius Festus
role: Roman governor to whom Paul appealed to Caesar
whenBasis: The reign as the rulers' data dates it, from sources outside the Bible.
summary: Felix's successor as governor of Judea. Three days after arriving he went up to Jerusalem, where the chief priests asked him to bring Paul there for trial, meaning to ambush him. Festus heard the case at Caesarea and, wishing to do the Jews a favour, asked Paul if he would go up to Jerusalem to be tried. Paul answered, “I appeal to Caesar!” and Festus replied, “To Caesar you will go!” He laid the case before King Agrippa, and during Paul's defence exclaimed that his great learning was driving him mad.
body: He tells Agrippa the charges were only about their own religion and a certain Jesus who had died, whom Paul affirmed to be alive, and that he has nothing definite to write to the emperor.

moments.text: “Are you willing to go up to Jerusalem?”

later.text: Josephus says he died in office; in the interval before his successor arrived, the high priest Ananus had James the brother of Jesus stoned, AD 62.
